items.name: react
items.purpose: The editor's rendering library. Every view is a React component; the shell holds the loaded documents as component state.
items.requirements: Renders a component tree to the DOM and re-renders it on state change. Must render a 250-row register table without a perceptible delay on a mid-range laptop. State updates must be applied in the order they are made, since document edits are sequential.
items.runtime: A browser supporting ES2020. No server-side rendering is used.
items.limitations: Rendering is not synchronous with state updates; code that assumes an edit is visible on the next line is wrong. React 18 concurrent features are not used.
items.maintenance: Actively maintained by Meta with a large contributor base and a published release policy. If it were abandoned, the editor would continue to work against the pinned version indefinitely; migration would be a rewrite of the view layer and is the largest single replacement risk in the product.

items.name: react-dom
items.purpose: Binds React to the browser DOM, and provides the portal used to render a row menu outside its table.
items.requirements: Mounts a React tree into a DOM node. `createPortal` must render into a node outside the parent's DOM hierarchy while keeping it inside the React tree — the row menu depends on this to escape a stacking context.
items.runtime: A browser supporting ES2020; versioned in lockstep with react.
items.limitations: Must match the react version exactly.

items.name: react-markdown
items.purpose: Renders the architecture document and each detailed-design section body from markdown, with an image handler that substitutes inline SVG diagrams.
items.requirements: Renders CommonMark to React elements. Must not execute or emit raw HTML from the document, since a specification is authored by several people and may be edited through a server. Must allow the image renderer to be replaced, which is how diagrams are placed inline.
items.limitations: Does not render arbitrary HTML by design; GitHub-flavoured tables require the remark-gfm plugin. Rendering is not incremental — a very large document re-renders whole.
items.maintenance: Part of the unified/remark collective, widely used and actively released. Replaceable at moderate cost: the markdown boundary is two components, both of which take the document as a string.

items.name: remark-gfm
items.purpose: Adds GitHub-flavoured markdown — principally tables — to the rendered architecture and design documents.
items.requirements: Parses GFM tables, strikethrough and task lists. Tables are the requirement that matters: the design documents use them heavily.
items.limitations: Does not implement every GitHub extension; footnote rendering differs from GitHub in detail.
items.maintenance: As react-markdown; same collective and release cadence.

items.name: @uiw/react-codemirror
items.purpose: The markdown editor for the architecture document and detailed-design section bodies — a React wrapper around CodeMirror 6.
items.requirements: Presents a text editor bound to a string, reporting every change. Must not reformat, normalise or otherwise alter text the author did not type: a specification document must round-trip through the editor byte for byte.
items.runtime: react 18+, and the CodeMirror 6 packages it depends on.
items.limitations: A wrapper: CodeMirror configuration beyond the exposed props requires reaching through to the underlying extension API.
items.maintenance: A single-maintainer wrapper over a well-maintained core, which is the risk. If it were abandoned, CodeMirror 6 could be used directly at moderate cost; the wrapper is convenience rather than capability.

items.name: @codemirror/lang-markdown
items.purpose: Markdown syntax highlighting inside the editor.
items.requirements: Highlights markdown syntax. Presentation only: it must never alter the document text.
items.limitations: Highlighting only; no linting or formatting.
items.maintenance: CodeMirror is maintained by its original author with a long and stable release history.

items.name: @dnd-kit (core, sortable, utilities)
items.requirements: Reports a drag from one list position to another, by item id, with keyboard as well as pointer input. Must not itself mutate the list — the shell applies the reorder, so a failed or cancelled drag can leave no trace.
items.limitations: Reordering only; no cross-list dragging or drop-target validation is used.
items.maintenance: Actively maintained and the de-facto standard since react-beautiful-dnd was deprecated. If abandoned, the outline falls back to the move-up and move-down controls already present, which is why they were kept.

items.name: ajv
items.purpose: Validates every document against its JSON Schema. This is the only component on which the correctness of the contract depends directly.
items.requirements: Validates a document against JSON Schema draft-07 and reports every violation, not merely the first, with a path identifying the offending field. A document it accepts must genuinely satisfy the schema: a false accept would let a malformed specification through governance.
items.runtime: Node 18+ or a browser supporting ES2020.
items.limitations: Reports structure only; policy such as referential integrity is not expressible in the schema and is enforced separately in the governance module.
items.maintenance: Long-established and widely depended upon, though release cadence has slowed. A false accept would be the worst failure in the product, which is why the schemas are also exercised directly by fixtures rather than trusted through ajv alone.

items.name: bootstrap
items.purpose: Base stylesheet for the editor. Layout and component classes only; SpecPad's own token layer is imported after it and overrides appearance.
items.requirements: Provides the grid, table, form-control, label, button and panel classes the views use. No JavaScript from Bootstrap is loaded.
items.runtime: A browser; no jQuery, since the JavaScript component library is not used.
items.limitations: Version 3 is no longer developed. Its visual defaults are dated, which is why the theme layer overrides them; and it predates CSS custom properties, so theming is done in SpecPad's own layer rather than Bootstrap's.
items.maintenance: End of life since 2019-07-24: no further releases will be made. Accepted deliberately — a stylesheet cannot develop new defects, and the JavaScript components that held the security-relevant issues are not loaded. Replacement by the token layer is scheduled work rather than contingency.
items.endOfLifeSource: https://blog.getbootstrap.com/2019/07/24/bootstrap-3-4-1-and-4-3-1/ — Bootstrap 3 reached end of life with 3.4.1; no further releases.

items.name: git
items.purpose: Every durable operation. The skill reads history through it, and the server clones, checks out, commits, rebases and pushes through it. SpecPad has no other store.
items.requirements: Supports sparse-checkout in cone mode, worktrees, rebase with an inspectable index, and push. Sparse-checkout is a security control here, not an optimisation: without it a working copy could contain application source. Command output must be stable enough to parse for status and conflict stages.
items.runtime: A POSIX or Windows host with the git binary on PATH, and credentials for the remote.
items.limitations: Invoked as a subprocess, so it is a process boundary rather than a library: errors arrive as exit codes and text. Behaviour varies slightly across versions, which is why every invocation goes through one runner.
items.maintenance: Maintained by a broad community with a predictable release cadence and long support history. Not replaceable: git is the product's premise rather than a dependency, and SpecPad would not exist in this form without it.

items.name: Node.js
items.purpose: Runs the self-hosted server and the skill's tooling. The server uses only the standard library — http, fs, path, crypto, child_process — and declares no runtime dependencies of its own.
items.requirements: Provides an HTTP server, filesystem access, subprocess execution and SHA-256 hashing. Must sustain server-sent event streams that stay open for hours without the connection being recycled underneath the application.
items.runtime: A supported operating system; a container image is provided.
items.limitations: Single-threaded per process: a long synchronous operation blocks every request, which is why git calls are asynchronous throughout.
items.maintenance: LTS lines are supported for 30 months with a published schedule, so end of support is knowable in advance rather than discovered. Node 20, which this register previously named, reached end of life on 2026-04-30; the supported floor is now 22 LTS (end of life 2027-04-30). Moving the floor is a version bump and a CI matrix change, since only the standard library is used.
